data.title: bn-52i6: HLC receive rule for the local clock

data.reason: HLC receive rule is sound: cap is relative to current now (bounded, self-heals within 1h), observe only raises, next_timestamp stays monotonic, clock-file errors warn only. New tests fail without the change and are not flaky. 242 related bones-core tests pass. Non-blocking: (1) delete, assign/unassign, undo use raw db::open_projection, dep rm never opens the projection, TUI actions use Connection::open, so these skip the observe step. ADR-006 says all write commands do this, which overstates it. (2) observe_timestamp does read-then-write on the clock file without ShardLock, and fs::write is not atomic. An interleaving with next_timestamp can lower the clock, and a torn read parses to 0. Impact is small: it loses monotonicity only when the wall clock also steps back or the clock holds an observed lead. Suggest taking ShardLock (try-acquire) in observe, or an atomic rename write. (3) An up-to-date projection at upgrade never observes old future-dated events until new events arrive.

LGTM at HEAD: reviewer LGTM on 7be12108; follow-up applies its note 1 (delete/assign/undo/dep rm now ensure_projection before timestamping) and note 2's torn-read fix (rename write). just check passes.
